identification: Single pale, long live-edge timber slab with bark edges, a few knots and checks, chalked 1133 23/10/26. In the photo the timber looks pale to mid-brown, ring-porous, more like ash, elm or oak than true walnut (walnut unconfirmed). Roughly 1.8 m long and narrow-waisted, one photo only. Gowans uses 'walnut' loosely for many slabs.

viewing_check: Check species (smell, end grain, colour on a fresh scratch: ash/elm/oak versus walnut), the real length, width and thickness, whether it is air-dried or still wet, and the depth of the checks, any rot or insect holes at the bark edges. Photograph both faces and the end grain.
rate_note: All AUD, no conversion. Gowans prices are hammer; add 19.8% premium.
